newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht down late after stock market fall.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht down late after stock market fall.

text.p: The baht weakened in late dealings to 25.451-25.454 against the dollar on Monday from 25.444-25.447 early as foreign investors unloaded the Thai currency after the stock market plummetted, dealers said.
Speculators shaken by the stock market fall to its lowest in over three years moved into dollars, they added.

"There was strong bid for both spot and forward dollar today. People also speculated there was possible outflow of foreign funds following heavy selling in the stock market by foreign investors," said one currency dealer.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 10.00/11.00 satangs per dollar late from 9.00/9.50 earlier on strong demand for forward dollars, dealers said.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.45 to the dollar against 25.44 on Friday.
The Thai overnight interbank rate was lower to 6.00-7.00 percent late from 8.00 earlier on higher money supply after central bank reserve requirements passed on Monday, dealers said.
The interbank rate of 6.00-7.00 percent was the lowest level since August 29 when the interbank rate was at 6.25-6.50.
"Commercial banks were pouring their excess funds into the market late afternoon after the reserve requirement passed," said one dealer at a European bank.
